paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me: David runs, but he doesn't run empty. The king is leaving his own city, and he still hands the whole thing to the LORD. He says, "If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring me back…" (2 Samuel 15:25), and then he sends the ark of the covenant of God back to Jerusalem instead of dragging it along like a lucky charm. He knows the LORD isn't a thing you carry. He's the One you trust.

Then watch what David does with his hands while he's trusting. He weeps, he walks barefoot, and he prays, "O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness!" (2 Samuel 15:31). In the very same stretch, he sends Hushai back to Jerusalem with a job to do. Praying and planning are NOT enemies, friend. I have prayed over a batch of dough and STILL set the timer.

So when your own morning falls apart, here's the takeaway. Be honest about how much it hurts, ask the LORD for what you need, and then take the next faithful step in front of you. Ittai shows it too: when David gave him an easy way out, he said, "wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there will your servant be!" (2 Samuel 15:21). Loyalty shows up on the hard road, and this story is nowhere near over.
